description: Add the shared DocumentCache cache-write/conditional-acknowledgement contract in the DMS backend/core boundary near the existing DocumentCache materializer and target-context contracts. Define the request model with resolved target context, DocumentId, optional selected RequiredContentVersion for diagnostics, caller purpose values for DurableWorkProjection and DirectFill, optional DocumentCacheMaterializationCandidate, and cancellation. Define a bounded result/outcome model that represents already-current acknowledgement, candidate-written acknowledgement, needs-materialization, lifecycle or latch fence, source missing/deleted, stale-candidate suppression, missing-work or work-mismatch anomalies with Tracking versus Rebuilding distinction, cache-ahead latch set, cache-ahead disappeared, racing-writer lost, exhausted retry budget, caller-aborted retry, delete-race retry exhaustion, and deterministic invariant/target failure. Add guard logic for invalid enum values, nonpositive versions, candidate DocumentId mismatch as a programming error, and matching-version candidate metadata mismatch as an invariant/target failure.
acceptance-criteria: One shared writer interface is available for later 18-04 projector and 18-05 direct-fill integrations without exposing a cache-only write API.
The writer request treats selected RequiredContentVersion as diagnostic context only and does not let it authorize cache DML or work acknowledgement.
The outcome model is bounded, typed, and covers every story-listed outcome including direct-fill use of the same result model.

Candidate DocumentId mismatch is rejected as a programming error before provider work; ContentVersion mismatch is represented as stale suppression; matching-version UUID or resource metadata mismatch is represented as deterministic invariant/target failure.
Contracts reuse the existing resolved target context and DocumentCacheMaterializationCandidate types instead of duplicating materializer-owned data.

description: Implement a provider-independent pure classification/action selector for current source/cache/work observations. The selector should consume the durable S/C/W classification plus lifecycle state, cache-ahead latch, caller purpose, candidate metadata comparison, and whether the writer is operating in Tracking or Rebuilding. It should choose only abstract actions and outcomes; it must not perform DML, target resolution, materialization, lifecycle administration, repair, or logging side effects.
acceptance-criteria: The selector maps source missing, C greater than S, S equals C equals W, C equals S with W absent, W equals S with cache absent/behind and current candidate, W equals S with cache absent/behind and no candidate, W equals S with stale candidate, W not equal S, and cache absent/behind with W absent to the story-required actions.

Cache-ahead is the only relationship that requests the incident latch flow; stale candidates, work mismatches, missing work, missing source rows, lifecycle fences, and duplicate writers do not request latch mutation.
Tracking missing-work anomalies and possible unseeded Rebuilding baseline rows are represented distinctly while both avoid cache DML and acknowledgement.
For both DurableWorkProjection and DirectFill purposes, cache absent or behind with no current matching work selects no cache DML even when a current candidate is supplied.
Equal-version acknowledgement is selected even when the supplied candidate is absent or stale.
The selector carries an expectedContentVersion for later acknowledgement when an action depends on a current S observation.

description: Add a cache-writer retry adapter that reuses the existing DeadlockRetry settings and semantics without routing through API handler result unions. The adapter should classify provider deadlock, serialization, lock-timeout, and equivalent transient failures for both PostgreSQL and SQL Server, replay the complete cache-write/conditional-acknowledgement transaction attempt on each retry, honor cancellation, surface exhausted-budget and caller-aborted writer outcomes, and emit sanitized retry diagnostics.
acceptance-criteria: DeadlockRetry MaxRetryAttempts, BaseDelayMilliseconds, jitter, retry-disabled behavior, transient-provider classification, and logging semantics are reused for cache writer attempts.
Every retry executes the complete writer attempt including state-row lock, S/C/W classification, cache DML when applicable, acknowledgement, and cache-ahead reclassification when applicable.
The writer does not retry only the final acknowledgement statement, enqueue trigger, or any post-commit fragment.
Non-transient provider failures and deterministic invariant failures are not retried as provider concurrency events.
Retry logs and metrics omit DocumentId, DocumentUuid, DocumentJson, request body content, authorization data, and unbounded resource labels.

description: Implement the PostgreSQL cache-writer transaction adapter. Each main attempt should open a short transaction, acquire the DocumentCacheState singleton with FOR SHARE through commit, verify lifecycle Tracking or Rebuilding with a clear CacheAheadRecoveryRequired latch, classify current Document, ResourceKey, DocumentCache, and DocumentProjectionWork for the input DocumentId in one provider-consistent statement, and execute parameterized cache and acknowledgement DML based only on the current classification and candidate predicates.
acceptance-criteria: Classification is anchored on the input DocumentId and left joins dms.Document, dms.ResourceKey, dms.DocumentCache, and dms.DocumentProjectionWork in one statement.

The transaction does not deliberately lock DocumentProjectionWork before accessing dms.DocumentCache and the parent dms.Document/ResourceKey rows needed by foreign-key and UUID/resource validation, and the adapter documents the PostgreSQL lock order used for duplicate writers and enqueue/acknowledge races.

Healthy candidate writes use one application-issued INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT (DocumentId) DO UPDATE statement that repeats current source, ResourceKey, work, candidate UUID, candidate ContentVersion, ProjectName, ResourceName, and ResourceVersion predicates.

Accepted candidate writes populate StreamEtag, LastModifiedAt, and DocumentJson from the materializer candidate as cache payload values, with LastModifiedAt remaining diagnostic/payload metadata rather than a freshness or ordering predicate.
The conflict update only advances lower cache ContentVersion rows and updates ComputedAt with a provider UTC timestamp only when cache content changes.

Final acknowledgement is a separate DELETE from dms.DocumentProjectionWork that binds DocumentId and expectedContentVersion and requires current source, cache, and work all still equal that expected version.
If this attempt writes cache but the final conditional acknowledgement affects zero rows, the whole transaction rolls back and returns a race-lost or retryable outcome.
Equal-version acknowledgement performs no cache DML and does not refresh ComputedAt.
Post-delete FK or UUID validation failures are treated as retryable delete races under the writer retry policy.

description: Implement the SQL Server cache-writer transaction adapter with behavior equivalent to the PostgreSQL adapter. Each main attempt should use a short transaction, take an exact-key shared HOLDLOCK on dms.DocumentCacheState through commit, verify lifecycle Tracking or Rebuilding with a clear latch, classify source/cache/work through one current statement, and apply SQL Server specific parameterized cache and acknowledgement DML.
acceptance-criteria: Classification is anchored on the input DocumentId and joins current dms.Document, dms.ResourceKey, dms.DocumentCache, and dms.DocumentProjectionWork in one provider-consistent statement.

The transaction does not deliberately lock DocumentProjectionWork before accessing dms.DocumentCache and the parent dms.Document/ResourceKey rows needed by foreign-key and UUID/resource validation, and the adapter documents the SQL Server lock order used for duplicate writers and enqueue/acknowledge races.
Healthy candidate writes use application-issued UPDATE then INSERT statements for a single DocumentId rather than MERGE.
The insert path takes an exact-key UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK probe on dms.DocumentCache before inserting to serialize duplicate absent-row writers.
UPDATE and INSERT sources repeat current source, ResourceKey, work, candidate UUID, candidate ContentVersion, ProjectName, ResourceName, and ResourceVersion predicates.

Accepted candidate writes populate StreamEtag, LastModifiedAt, and DocumentJson from the materializer candidate as cache payload values, with LastModifiedAt remaining diagnostic/payload metadata rather than a freshness or ordering predicate.
ComputedAt uses sysutcdatetime() only when cache content changes; equal-version acknowledgement performs no cache update.
Final acknowledgement deletes only matching DocumentProjectionWork where current source, cache, and work all still equal the expectedContentVersion.
Cache DML and acknowledgement commit together or roll back together under all acknowledgement race outcomes and delete races.

description: Implement the cache-ahead incident flow shared by both provider adapters. When the main transaction classifies current C greater than S, it should commit or roll back with no cache write and no acknowledgement, then start a short incident transaction that obtains the state row exclusively, revalidates lifecycle Tracking or Rebuilding with the latch still clear, re-runs current S/C/W classification, and sets CacheAheadRecoveryRequired only if C greater than S remains current.
acceptance-criteria: The incident transaction sets the latch only after exclusive state-row lock, lifecycle revalidation, clear-latch revalidation, and one current S/C/W reclassification.

Lifecycle changes, missing/unreadable state, or an already-set latch between the main transaction and incident transaction return a lifecycle/latch-fenced outcome without cache DML or acknowledgement.
If C greater than S disappears on recheck, the writer returns a cache-ahead-disappeared outcome and leaves lifecycle, latch, cache, and work unchanged.
The incident flow is a bounded safety continuation after C greater than S, using a short incident timeout rather than ordinary work-item or direct-fill timeout.

If shutdown or provider cancellation prevents the incident flow from starting or finishing after C greater than S, the result distinguishes cache-ahead-unconfirmed caller abort from ordinary caller abort.

description: Add a production-safe, test-disabled-by-default transaction fault-injection observer for the cache writer. Provide named hook points after main state lock and S/C/W classification before cache DML, after successful cache DML before acknowledgement, after successful acknowledgement before commit, and after cache-ahead latch update before the incident transaction commits. The observer must be injectable in tests, absent or no-op in production by default, and must not create after-commit hooks or process-local durable correctness latches.
acceptance-criteria: All four story-required hook points are available with stable names and bounded context that excludes document identifiers and payloads.
Tests can close the provider connection or force rollback at each hook point to exercise crash-window behavior.
Default production registration is no-op and cannot alter writer behavior unless a test explicitly supplies an observer.
Hook context labels are sanitized and bounded to provider, normalized target key, caller purpose, lifecycle, and outcome-style data.
No after-commit hook or process-local durable latch is added as correctness evidence.

description: Add sanitized cache-writer metrics and minimal same-document enqueue/acknowledgement contention instrumentation. The writer should emit counters for bounded outcomes and histograms for full transaction duration, cache DML duration, acknowledgement duration, retry duration or attempts, and writer-side wait on same-document canonical writers. Add or wire minimal canonical write/enqueue-path instrumentation so canonical writers blocked by acknowledgement transactions contribute to the same sanitized contention metric family.
acceptance-criteria: Metrics labels are bounded to provider, normalized target key, caller purpose, lifecycle, and outcome where applicable.
Metrics and logs never include DocumentId, DocumentUuid, DocumentJson, request body content, authorization data, or unbounded resource labels.
Writer-side histograms measure transaction duration, cache DML duration, acknowledgement duration, and same-document canonical-writer wait.
Canonical write/enqueue instrumentation records same-document contention caused by acknowledgement transactions without adding a second retry layer around canonical writes.

Outcome counters distinguish successful acknowledgements, candidate writes, stale suppression, anomalies, lifecycle fences, cache-ahead flows, race-lost results, retry exhaustion, caller abort, and invariant failures.
